_notes: ONE LADDER FOR EVERY FACTION (Kyle, 2026-10-27: 'keep the wow tiers of rep... there will be a lot').
The tiers below are the WoW-standard eight and they are defined ONCE, here, shared by every faction.
A faction block carries only who it is, where its reputation comes from, and what standing buys - never
its own ladder. That is what lets one UI tab list fifty factions without fifty different scales, and it
means adding a faction is a block of data and nothing else.
Thresholds are cumulative from Neutral, exactly as WoW: Friendly 3000, Honored 9000, Revered 21000,
Exalted 42000. Negative standing is defined too - nothing in the game drives rep down yet, but the
ladder has to support it before something does, or the first hostile faction rewrites this file.
THE NUMBERS DO TWO DIFFERENT JOBS. A zone's quests are worth enough together to carry a player into
Revered - that is the real path and the one that tells the story. Exalted is finished on kills, and
only kills from enemies the faction has an actual stake in. There is deliberately no flat 'dungeon
mobs give rep' rule: it would make the optimal play farming the easiest trash in the easiest room,
and killing a mushroom should not earn standing with a library.

crimson_codex.name: The Crimson Codex
crimson_codex.description: Blood elf arcanists who went down a hole beneath the Ruins of Dalaran and never came back up.

leader.title: Codex-Master
leader.name: Ilarien Duskwaking
leader.line: Eleven thousand entries and the cavern keeps handing me things I have no column for. Do not take that as an invitation.

crimson_codex._lore_note: Shown on the faction's detail panel. Written as the Codex would have it written - they are the ones keeping the record, and they are not neutral about themselves.
lore: The fissure opened in ground the blood elves had already surveyed. One of them put a boot through what should have been solid rock above the Ruins of Dalaran, and the hole went down past the reach of every lamp they were carrying.

Below it they found a cavern wide enough to hold weather, lit by something hanging at the centre of it that none of them has reached. They have been down there ever since. They call it a find rather than a discovery, because a find is something that was already there, waiting.

Their work is the index. Every crystal, every column, every stand of fungus gets a number and a place in the ledger. Lately the ledger has begun to fail them. There is Dalaran stone far beneath Dalaran that no cart ever carried down. There is crystal growing in figures too exact for honest stone. And under the Sporefall something has been reading their notes through the mould in their own camp, and writing back.

They are precise, dry, and a good deal more frightened than they let on. They also came through the same change you did. Nobody in Kael's Bastion has an older claim on any of it, and every one of them knows it.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. kill_boss objectives pay the boss rate; the named capstones pay more.

_comment: Only enemies the Codex has a stake in. Dissidents are ex-colleagues, Interlopers are rivals for
the same dig, Revenants sit on the prize, and the Deep Bloom is the thing reading them back.
The wildlife pays nothing, however deep the cave it lives in.
What standing actually buys. These are the GATES - they work, and they are not displayed on the
faction panel (Kyle, 2026-10-27: the panel is information only). Rewards will eventually span gear,
crafting recipes, recruits, quests and whole zones unlocked, so a reward ladder is not worth drawing
until it can show all of that honestly.

orgrimmar.name: Orgrimmar
orgrimmar.description: The orc capital: raised fast out of red stone and ship timber by people who could not afford to be particular.

leader.title: Warchief
leader.name: Thrall
leader.line: We were given nothing. We took a desert and made a home of it. I will not stand here and apologise for the taking.

lore: The Horde came ashore in Durotar with what it could carry. Orgrimmar went up out of red stone and the bones of the ships, and the city still looks like what it is.

Thrall holds it. He was born in chains and got his people out of them, and it left him careful in a way that sits oddly on a warchief - he would sooner keep what the Horde has than reach for more. There are voices in the city that disagree, and they are not quiet.

The city's regard is a ledger kept by quartermasters, not by singers. Who held the Barrens road. Who went down into the Chasm when the Burning Blade came up out of it. Who was on the wall when it mattered.

When the world changed, Orgrimmar opened its gates to the people it threw up, faster than anywhere else on the continent and with less argument. Thrall has never explained that in public. Those who were in the camps with him do not need him to.

kill_rep._comment: The Horde's standing enemies in its own territory - the cult under the city, the centaur on the Barrens road, the quilboar in the fields, the harpies on the ridge.

darkspear_tribe.name: The Darkspear Tribe
darkspear_tribe.description: Jungle trolls who were down to their last island, and have never once let anyone call what happened next a rescue.

leader.title: Elder
leader.name: Kang'ari
leader.line: We been run off dis water before, mon. We came back. Dat is most of what you need to know about us.

lore: The Darkspear were down to their last island when the Horde found them. It was a bargain, struck between two peoples who had nothing, and the trolls have kept their half of it with a thoroughness that embarrasses larger nations.
Then Zalazane took the isles. He went through the tribe with hex and voodoo until their own kin came out of the surf at them, and the Darkspear pulled back to the mainland and began again.
They do not say the isles are lost. They say the ones still out on the water are not back yet. That is a different thing, and they will correct you on it.
The tribe keeps its own spiritwalkers, its own trainers, its own account of who stood with them when it was bad. That account is older than the Horde's and it is not the same list.

kill_rep._comment: Zalazane's hexed and the naga on the reefs - the two things keeping the tribe off its own islands.

the_forsaken.name: The Forsaken
the_forsaken.description: The dead of Lordaeron, who woke with their minds intact and took the ruin of their capital back.

leader.title: Banshee Queen
leader.name: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner
leader.line: We were not given our freedom. I took it, and I will not be asked to be grateful for a thing I had to tear loose.

lore: The Scourge raised Lordaeron's dead and set them walking. Then the hold on them slipped, and what straightened up in the ruins remembered everything - names, houses, the faces of their families, and exactly what had been done to them.

They took the undercroft beneath the palace and made a country of it. The throne room overhead still has the old king's blood dried into the floor. Nobody down there calls that tragic. They call it theirs.

The Apothecarium sits at the heart of the city and worries everyone, allies included. They are the only people on the continent studying the plague that made them. Ask them why and you will be told: a cure. Read the ledgers and you may arrive somewhere else.

What they will not forgive is the Scarlet Crusade, who kill them on sight for the crime of having been murdered, and the cults still working for the thing that did it. Standing with the Forsaken is mostly a tally of how many of those two you have put back in the ground.
They are tired, blackly funny, and very hard to impress. They have been dead a while. Little is new.

kill_rep._comment: The Scarlet Crusade, who kill them on sight, and the cults still serving the thing that made them.

steamwheedle_cartel.name: The Steamwheedle Cartel
steamwheedle_cartel.description: Goblin traders who will sell to anyone, protect no one, and keep a port open through wars that shut everything else.

leader.title: Boss
leader.name: Gazlowe
leader.line: Neutral ain't a principle, friend. It's a business model, and it's the only one that keeps a port open when everyone on both sides wants it.

lore: The Cartel is not a nation and has never pretended to be. It is a company with harbours, and those harbours are the only stretches of coast where a Horde ship and an Alliance ship tie up at the same pier and nothing happens.

The neutrality is the product. Bring a war into Ratchet and the goblins will not take a side. They will put you on a boat, bill your faction for the disruption, and have the dock working again by the evening tide.

Gazlowe runs the port, and runs it better than the margins deserve. He has turned down three offers to move the whole operation somewhere richer. No goblin will explain that, and more than a few have tried to buy the explanation out of him.

Their regard is bought rather than earned and they are honest about it. Pirates on the water and bandits on the Barrens road cost the Cartel money. Anyone who brings that number down is good for business, and good for business is as near to friendship as Ratchet deals in.

kill_rep._comment: Whatever interrupts trade: pirates on the water, bandits on the Barrens road. The Cartel pays per head and does not care about your politics.

thunder_bluff.name: Thunder Bluff
thunder_bluff.description: A people still answering to the name of a city that is no longer standing.
thunder_bluff.home_name: Camp Taurajo, the Southern Barrens - in exile

leader.title: Elder
leader.name: Longtread
leader.line: The seat is his. I stand near it. I will go on standing near it until somebody puts a reason in my hand.

thunder_bluff._leader_note: Longtread speaks for the tauren and holds no title. Cairne was LOST when the city fell - never found, never buried - so the office is not vacant so much as unresolved, and taking it would be a ruling nobody is willing to make.
lore: Thunder Bluff stood on four rock spires above Mulgore and had never been taken by anyone. When the world changed, nothing climbed those spires. The ground beneath them went, and the city went with it.

What Mulgore is now has no good name. The grass still grows. The sky is still up there. Everything else about that plain is wrong, and the things walking it kill war parties without breaking stride. Four times the tauren have gone back for the spires. They will talk about three of those.

Cairne Bloodhoof was in the city when it fell. Nobody saw him after. Nothing has been found since - no body, no sign, nothing to bury - so the chieftain's seat stands empty. Elder Longtread speaks for the tauren and has turned down the title every time it has been put to him, because taking it would settle a question that is not settled.

They are guests now. Camp Taurajo, the warbands in the southern Barrens, and more of them in other people's towns every season. Every nation that took them in did it without conditions and without being asked twice, and the tauren have been thanking them for it ever since, which carries its own weight.
And they are still called Thunder Bluff. There is no Thunder Bluff. They have had this pointed out, agree politely, and go on using the name.

kill_rep._comment: What presses on the ground they have left: quilboar raiding the camps, and the Bael'dun dwarves digging a plain that is not theirs while the tauren watch a worse one from a distance.

rewards._comment: No gates authored yet. When Mulgore is built as the level 60 zone, this is where its access and its rewards belong.

booty_bay_authority.name: The Booty Bay Port Authority
booty_bay_authority.description: A goblin harbour that stopped being a franchise and started behaving like a government.

leader.title: Baron
leader.name: Baron Revilgaz
leader.line: The Cartel will tell you this is their port. Let them. They are four thousand miles away and I am standing on it.

booty_bay_authority._lore_note: Shown on the faction's detail panel. Written from the harbour's side of the argument, because the harbour is the one winning it.
lore: There is no road into Stranglethorn. The range closed the land route and never opened it again, which left two ways in: an airship berth the Horde flew in over the top, and this cove.

That made Booty Bay the only deep-water harbour still joining anything to anything, and a harbour in that position stops taking instructions. The Baron did not declare anything. He simply began deciding which hulls left on which tide, and after the third season nobody was asking Ratchet.

The Steamwheedle Cartel has not formally lost the port and will say so at length. Factor Weezel still signs the manifests, still files them, and still gets a polite reply. The replies do not change what sails.

What the Authority sells is the same thing the Cartel always sold - a pier where two enemies can tie up and nothing happens - except that here it is enforced rather than negotiated. The bruisers are the law, the Baron is the court, and the tariff is not up for discussion. People complain about the landing fee until the first time they need the harbour to hold.

quest_rep._comment: Honored is the ceiling on quests alone. Everything below is authored in Booty Bay and the southern jungle - the Authority does not pay for work done north of the Gurbashi, because north of the Gurbashi is Orgrimmar's problem.

kill_rep._comment: What costs the harbour money. Bloodsail on the water above all - a pirate in the shallows is a hull that does not arrive - plus the naga sitting on the drowned terraces the Authority would very much like to salvage. Jungle wildlife pays nothing: it has never cost anyone a cargo.

rewards._comment: No gates authored yet. The system supports them; the content is not written.

dungeon_rep._comment: A dungeon BOSS kill pays 75. Trash pays nothing, so the unit of progress is a boss. The Authority takes bets on the Gurbashi and has a direct interest in who wins.

the_ashclaim.name: The Ashclaim
the_ashclaim.description: Dark Iron dwarves and goblins reclaiming a city that is legally one dwarf's and practically nobody's.

leader.title: Thane of Khaz Varun
leader.name: Durgan Ashhold
leader.line: My great-grandfather's hall is four hundred feet down and full of things that used to be my cousins. The goblins have given me a figure for clearing it. I have signed it. Do not ask me what it was.

the_ashclaim._lore_note: Written as the Ashclaim would have it written - a prospectus, not a history. The thane supplies the claim and the goblins supply everything else, and both of them describe that arrangement as generous of themselves.
lore: Khaz Varun went dark long before the Integration, and the Ashholds have carried the deed from hall to rented room to a bunk on a goblin barge for as long as anyone has bothered to count.
What changed is that the sea route opened. A deed nobody could reach is a story; a deed four days from Saltspur is an asset, and the goblins can read an asset at a distance.

So the thane holds the claim and the underwriters hold the paper on the claim, and a wharf went up on the north-east shore inside a season. The hold behind it is built from the old city's own salvaged stone, which the dwarves consider a homecoming and the goblins consider freight they did not have to buy.

Neither half of the Ashclaim agrees on what the isle is for. The thane wants his ancestors' hall emptied of whatever is living in it now. The underwriters want the foundry lit and earning, and have observed in writing that those two things are not the same dig.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. Matches the Crimson Codex rates so nothing new needs tuning.
